stories.title: Watchdog must not report healthy while the display is frozen
acceptance: LIVE PROOF 2026-08-20: `WEDGED -- 101 markers` at one tick and `healthy; markers=84` at the next. The threshold (100) sits INSIDE the observed band (84-101), so the watchdog's verdict is a coin-flip on a wedged display

an absolute marker COUNT threshold inside the signal's own operating band cannot separate wedged from healthy -- the detector needs a discriminator that does (rate/delta/stall-time), not a retuned constant. Same lesson as Spool's coolant band: a bare threshold set inside a cycling signal's oscillation range always misfires

ENUMERATE AND ADDRESS ALL FOUR watchdog defects from section 3 of Atlas's 08-17 finding -- read the finding, list all four in completionNotes, and state the disposition of each. Do not fix one and close the story

stories.title: Plausibility gate -- a non-measurement must never wear data_source=real
acceptance: ONE story, not three: syncPending=0, the IMU all-zero frames and the latched magnetometer are the SAME defect -- a non-measurement wearing data_source='real'

TEST BIT-IDENTITY, NOT LOW VARIANCE (load-bearing). Every real sensor dithers +/-1 LSB even in a constant field, so N consecutive BIT-IDENTICAL samples cannot occur naturally. This needs NO magic threshold and CANNOT false-positive on a genuinely stationary vehicle. Proven 2026-08-20: stationary accel gave 743 distinct values in 90s; the magnetometer gave 1. A `variance < threshold` test would need a tuned number AND would false-positive when parked
route detections into the EXISTING failed-poll path (already proven honest) -- do NOT build a new silence mechanism
new reasons `sensor_mute` / `sensor_stale`, DISTINCT from `sensor_absent` -- the chip is enumerated and responding, which is a different fact

derived fields go typed-NA WITH their input: headingDeg is derived from the magnetometer, so a latched magnetometer must take headingDeg to NA -- today the F-127 Home face renders a fabricated heading on the primary card
syncPending must be fixed on BOTH layers -- the emitter emits null AND syncTile stops coercing null to 0 -- or it ships green and still reads `0 pending`
ruff/lint clean

validationCriteria.action: run the gate against a genuinely stationary vehicle for 90s
validationCriteria.outcome: NO false positive -- real sensors dither, so bit-identity does not trigger

validationCriteria.action: read the sync tile with the emitter returning null
validationCriteria.outcome: shows unknown/NA, never `0 pending`

conditionalOutcomes: The gate must stand ALONE to catch the NEXT sensor fault -- do NOT fold the magnetometer fix (US-565) into it.

stories.goal: As the operator, I want a stuck sensor to declare itself unavailable rather than publish a frozen value that looks live.
stories.pmSignOff: Marcus (PM) 2026-08-20 -- size L approved, NOT split. syncPending=0, the IMU all-zero frames and the latched magnetometer are ONE defect (a non-measurement wearing data_source='real'), and Atlas specified them as one story for that reason. Splitting by symptom would produce three narrow patches and no general guard -- and the guard is the point: it must catch the NEXT sensor fault, not these three. syncPending's two-layer fix (emitter emits null AND syncTile stops coercing to 0) is inseparable for the same reason -- either half alone ships green and still reads '0 pending'.

validation.validationMethod: V0.29 CLOSEOUT ORDER (Atlas, and he feels strongly about item 1): (1) US-560 apply the US-552 mode pin and verify fb0 = 480,320 -- it is cheap, it is owed anyway for F-127's in-car legibility check, and it is the LAST UNTESTED LEVER on the freeze; every freeze observation to date is at 720p/1080p, so the shipping configuration has never been tested. (2) US-561 watchdog defects -- resolution-independent, ship regardless. (3) US-562/563 drive_summary roll-up + schema defaults. (4) US-564 plausibility gate, then (5) US-565 magnetometer. THEN F-132 chrome (US-555..559), whose own acceptance is IN-CAR, seated, arm's length. The freeze ITSELF is deliberately NOT scoped here -- re-measure only after the mode pin lands.

outOfScope: THE FREEZE ITSELF -- re-measure after US-560 pins the mode. Every observation so far is at ~6x the shipping pixel count; scoping it now would chase a variable we can eliminate for one command plus a reboot.

GPIO6 single ownership (Atlas SPEC 2) -- DEFERRED WITH FLAG. Real safety gap (the operator has no way to know safe-shutdown protection is off, and powerwatch emits zero application lines so we are blind to whether it armed), but Atlas ordered it 4th of 5 and it explicitly does NOT fix the instant key-off death. Raised to the CIO as a judgment call, not silently dropped.
X1209 hold-up path / instant key-off death (P0 finding 8e726b1) -- CIO hardware domain, not a software story.

Kiosk modal-prompt gap (an automotive appliance must never show a WiFi dialog) -- filed, not a V0.29 blocker.
